children: Edgewell Personal Care swung to a profit in the recent quarter as sales rose, with the company's ongoing restructuring actions beginning to bear fruit.
The company on Thursday reported a fiscal fourth-quarter profit of $10.9 million, or 23 cents a share. That compares with a loss of $30.6 million, or 66 cents a share, a year earlier.
Stripping out certain one-time items, earnings came in at 78 cents a share, a penny higher than the expectations of analysts polled by FactSet.
Net sales climbed 3% to $484.1 million, ahead of Wall Street estimates for $479.9 million.
Chief Executive Rod Little said the quarterly results reflect continued growth in North America, a return to growth in international markets and improving performance across its core brands.
"We enter fiscal 2027 as a more focused business, with confidence in our plans to build on this progress, increase support behind our brands and improve profitability," he said.

The company will continue to take action to strengthen its operating model, simplify the business and improve manufacturing and supply-chain efficiencies, as significant cost and competitive pressures persist.

For the coming year. Edgewell guided for earnings of 90 cents to $1.20 a share, or $1.85 to $2.15 a share on an adjusted basis. Analysts were looking for earnings of $1.44 a share, as well as adjusted earnings of $1.98 a share.
Net sales are projected to increase between 0.4% and 2.4%. Wall Street modeled sales of $2.02 billion, up 1.2% from last year.
